components.name: Tool-call card
components.summary: Collapsed-by-default card that shows one tool invocation with its seven-state lifecycle, inputs and outputs.

anatomy.description: The card. Carries data-state (tool lifecycle) and data-effect (read | write | destroy).
The disclosure trigger. Whole row is pressable; aria-expanded lives here.
Tool-category glyph (search, file, terminal, browser). Decorative.
Humanised tool name plus target — "Searching the web for 'oklch contrast'", "Reading src/app.tsx". Never the raw function name.
State badge with text ("Running", "Completed", "Error"); colour is secondary.
Rotates on expand; rotation is paired with the header background change (LQ-STATE-02).
Collapsible region. Hidden by default except on error.
Arguments as highlighted JSON in type.family.mono; truncated with "show all" past 20 lines.
Result, error, or a registered generative-UI component. Never model-supplied HTML.
Retry (on error), Copy (on output), Approve / Deny (when approval-requested).

variants.guidance: Row is a single line with the summary (Claude Code style); card adds a visible border and padding. Grouped runs ("Searched 4 sources") are a row.
Drives data-effect and the status token so writes look different from reads without expansion (LQ-TOOL-02).

states.treatment: Status "Pending" in color.status.pending; name may still be arriving; shimmer on the name, opacity-only under reduced motion.
states.a11y: none until a name exists; then one announcement "Preparing {name}".

states.treatment: Status "Running" in color.status.running with a spinner; elapsed time after 10 s (LQ-WAIT-01).
states.a11y: aria-busy="true" on root; one polite announcement "Running {name}".

states.treatment: Body auto-expands; approval-prompt rendered inside; the card is outlined in color.status.warning.
states.a11y: Assertive announcement "Approval needed: {verb} {object}"; focus moves to the prompt.

states.treatment: Status "Approved" or "Denied"; the prompt collapses to one line recording the decision.
Status "Completed" in color.status.success; collapses to a one-line summary ("Read 3 files"); spinner removed.
states.a11y: aria-busy removed; one polite announcement "{name} complete".

states.treatment: Status "Error" in color.status.error with an icon; body auto-expands to show the message; Retry visible.
states.a11y: role="alert" on the message, not the whole card.

states.treatment: Status "Denied" in color.fg.muted; no output; one line explaining who denied it.
Header background shifts one step; chevron rotates; body visible.

states.treatment: Ring on the header button and on each action.
Header background one step.
Base.
Header inset.
none — a tool card is never disabled; it is denied or errored.

props.name: state
props.description: Rendered from the tool machine, never inferred from content (message-state-machine).

props.name: name
props.description: Humanised, with target. The implementation does not humanise; the caller does, so the mapping is one place.

props.name: output
props.description: A registered component (a framework element, a custom element, a DOM node) may be passed for generative UI.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Forced true by the implementation when state is output-error or approval-requested.

api.composition: Built from disclosure + badge + code-block + spinner + card. Output is a slot so a product can render its own component for a tool's result; the card never renders HTML strings.

accessibility.name: Root is labelled by the name part; the body is labelled by the header.

keyboard.action: Moves through header, then visible actions. Collapsed body contents are not in the tab order.

accessibility.focus: On approval-requested, focus moves to the approval prompt's safe option (Deny). On output-error, focus does not move; the alert role announces.
accessibility.announcements: Exactly one announcement per state change, polite except approval-requested (assertive). Batched when several cards change within 2 s (LQ-A11Y-01).

content.label: Humanised verb + target. "Searching the web for 'x'", "Reading src/app.tsx", "Running npm test". Group repeats: "Searched 4 sources".
content.voice: Progressive while running ("Reading"), past tense when done ("Read 3 files"), plain on error ("Couldn't read src/app.tsx: permission denied").
content.limits: Never the raw function name or a UUID in the visible name. Never "Processing…" without a target.

use_when: Any tool-using model or agent, one card per invocation, grouped when repeated.
avoid_when: Expanding every call by default (a wall of JSON).
Rendering model-supplied HTML as the output.
Showing a spinner without a name and target for more than 2 s (LQ-TOOL-01).

instead.when: Many steps over a long run that need scanning and jumping
The action needs a decision before it runs

exemplars: AI Elements Tool — the seven-state vocabulary with badges; adopt the names, collapse completed by default.
Claude Code — one-line tool summaries in the transcript; the row density variant.
CopilotKit — tool result rendered as a registered React component; the output slot.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers an action in the current context; the single most-used interactive component in any product.

anatomy.description: The native button. Carries every state attribute.
Optional icon before the label; decorative (aria-hidden).
Visible text. Required unless the button is icon-only, in which case use Icon Button instead.
Optional icon after the label; usually a chevron or external-link glyph.
Replaces the leading icon while loading. Width is reserved so the label does not shift.
Rendered by the focus-visible treatment, not a DOM node, but it is a part the grader looks for.

variants.guidance: One primary per view. Destructive is an emphasis, not a colour; it still obeys every state rule.
Size changes height, inset and label style together; never one without the others.

states.treatment: Base tokens for the chosen emphasis.
Background one step (color.bg.*-hover). Never move the element. Transition motion.duration.fast.
states.a11y: none — hover is not available to keyboard or touch and must never be the only cue.

states.treatment: 2px ring in color.border.focus with focus.ring.offset, ≥3:1 against component and page. Use :focus-visible, not :focus.
states.a11y: Implicit. Never outline none without a replacement (LQ-FOCUS-01).

states.treatment: Darken one step past hover or inset the surface; ~50ms so it feels immediate.
opacity.disabled, pointer-events none, hover/active responses removed. Keep legible.
states.a11y: `disabled` removes it from tab order. Prefer `aria-disabled="true"` (soft-disable) for anything a user might reasonably try, so the reason can be discovered.

states.treatment: In-place spinner that preserves width; label opacity reduced; re-submission blocked.
states.a11y: aria-busy="true"; announce start and finish politely from the surrounding region, not the button.

states.treatment: Persistent color.bg.selected plus a weight or border change. Only for toggle usage — see Toggle Button.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: Visual weight. Called `variant` in most libraries; Lacquer calls the axis by what it controls.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows the spinner, blocks activation, keeps width.

props.name: softDisabled
props.description: Keeps the button focusable so a tooltip can explain why it is unavailable.

props.name: type
props.description: Default is `button`, not `submit`, so a button inside a form never submits by accident.

events.name: press
events.description: Fired on click, Enter and Space. Not fired while loading or disabled.

api.composition: Icons are children, not props (`<Button><Icon/>Save</Button>`), so any icon set works and the label stays in the accessible name. Emphasis and size are props because they are closed sets the system owns. There is no `color` prop: destructive is an emphasis.

accessibility.name: From the label content. Icon-only buttons are a different component (icon-button) and require aria-label.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the button. Disabled (hard) buttons are skipped; soft-disabled are not.

accessibility.focus: Focus stays on the button after activation unless the action moves it deliberately (opening a dialog moves focus into the dialog).
accessibility.notes: A `div` with role="button" needs tabindex, Enter and Space handling and is still worse than the native element. The spec names no exception.

content.label: Verb first, then the object — "Save changes", "Delete 3 files". Sentence case. Three words or fewer when possible.
content.voice: Say what happens, not what the user should do. "Send" not "Click to send".
content.limits: Never "OK", "Yes", "No", "Submit", "Click here" when a specific verb is possible. Never ellipsis unless the button opens a dialog that asks for more input ("Export…").

use_when: Submitting, saving, opening a dialog, running an operation.
The action happens in the current context and does not change the URL.
avoid_when: The action navigates to a URL — that is a Link, even if it looks like a button.
The control has no visible label — that is an Icon Button.
The control stays pressed — that is a Toggle Button.
More than one primary button is visible in a view.

instead.when: It opens a menu of related actions

exemplars: GOV.UK Button — one primary per page, enforced in guidance; the clearest statement of emphasis discipline.
React Aria Button — press events unify mouse, touch, keyboard and screen-reader activation.

local.title: Never a div with onClick
local.statement: A button is a native `<button>`; a `div`, `span` or `a` without `href` carrying a click handler is a defect.

detect.static: div|span[onClick] without role=button, or any element with role=button that is not <button>.
detect.runtime: Press Enter and Space on the focused control; both must activate.

local.fix: Replace with `<button type="button">` and keep the classes.

local.title: Loading keeps width and blocks re-press
local.statement: While loading, the button keeps its enabled width, shows an in-place spinner, sets aria-busy="true" and ignores further presses.

detect.static: loading branch renders a spinner inside the button and sets aria-busy.
detect.runtime: Measure width before and during loading; press twice; the handler fires once.

local.fix: Reserve the icon slot for the spinner and gate the press handler on `loading`.

local.title: One primary per view

local.fix: Demote the others to secondary or tertiary; if two actions are equally important, neither is primary.

detect.runtime: Drive each state and diff computed styles against the enabled state; each must differ in at least one property.

resolved.title: No state by colour alone

resolved.title: Never remove focus without replacing it

detect.static: Class or style removes outline and no focus-visible ring class/rule exists on the same element.
detect.runtime: Tab to the element; the focused and unfocused screenshots must differ at ≥3:1 along the element's edge.

resolved.fix: Use `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2` (or the binding's equivalent) and keep `:focus` untouched.

resolved.title: Native element first
resolved.statement: Prefer the native element (button, a, select, details, input) until a product requirement makes it impossible; a div or span with a click handler and a role is a defect unless the spec names an exception.

detect.static: div|span with onClick/onKeyDown and no native equivalent in the subtree.

resolved.fix: Replace with the native element; keep the styling.

resolved.title: Every control has an accessible name
resolved.statement: Every interactive element has an accessible name from content, a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; placeholder text and title attributes do not count.

detect.static: Compute the accessible name per accname 1.2; empty is a failure.

resolved.fix: Add visible text, a <label>, or aria-label for icon-only controls.

resolved.title: No literal values
resolved.statement: Component styles read token roles only, through the binding's custom properties; no literal colours, radii, shadows, durations or z-indexes (`#7c3aed`, `oklch(…)`, `border-radius: 12px`, `z-index: 50`, `300ms`).
resolved.rationale: Tokens are the primer; the component is the finish. A literal value breaks every theme at once.

detect.static: A declaration on a component part sets colour, radius, shadow, duration or z-index to anything other than `var(--lq-…)` (or a utility class that does not resolve to a role through the binding).

resolved.fix: Replace with the role's custom property from the binding (see spec/bindings/html.yaml).

resolved.title: Parts are addressable
resolved.statement: Every anatomy part renders with `data-slot="<part>"` so docs, tests and the grader can target it without classes.

detect.static: For each anatomy part marked required, an element with that data-slot exists.

resolved.fix: Add data-slot to the part's root element.

resolved.rationale: Most "the UI looks unfinished" complaints are missing states, not missing components.

detect.static: For each interactive element, the stylesheet or class list defines treatments for :hover, :focus-visible, :active and [disabled] / [aria-disabled].
detect.runtime: Drive each state and diff computed styles against the enabled state; each must differ in at least one property.

resolved.fix: Add the missing state using the component's token deltas (see its states[] treatment).

resolved.title: No state by colour alone
resolved.statement: No state is expressed by colour alone; every state has a second channel (icon, weight, border, position or text).

detect.static: A state's class delta changes only color/background-color.
detect.runtime: Grayscale the screenshot of each state and check it still differs from enabled.

resolved.fix: Add an icon, border, weight or text change alongside the colour change.

resolved.title: Every state reaches the accessibility tree
resolved.statement: Every visible state has an ARIA expression or an explicit "none" in the spec; selected, expanded, invalid, busy and current are never visual-only.

detect.static: For each state the component declares, the matching attribute (aria-selected, aria-expanded, aria-invalid, aria-busy, aria-current, aria-checked) is present when the state is active.

resolved.fix: Set the attribute the APG pattern specifies; do not invent a new one.

resolved.title: Never remove focus without replacing it
resolved.statement: No `outline: none` / `outline-0` / `focus:outline-none` without a `:focus-visible` replacement that has ≥3:1 contrast against both the component and the page.

detect.static: Class or style removes outline and no focus-visible ring class/rule exists on the same element.
detect.runtime: Tab to the element; the focused and unfocused screenshots must differ at ≥3:1 along the element's edge.

resolved.fix: Use `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2` (or the binding's equivalent) and keep `:focus` untouched.

resolved.title: Native element first
resolved.statement: Prefer the native element (button, a, select, details, input) until a product requirement makes it impossible; a div or span with a click handler and a role is a defect unless the spec names an exception.

detect.static: div|span with onClick/onKeyDown and no native equivalent in the subtree.

resolved.fix: Replace with the native element; keep the styling.

resolved.title: Every control has an accessible name
resolved.statement: Every interactive element has an accessible name from content, a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; placeholder text and title attributes do not count.

detect.static: Compute the accessible name per accname 1.2; empty is a failure.

resolved.fix: Add visible text, a <label>, or aria-label for icon-only controls.

resolved.title: No literal values
resolved.statement: Component styles read token roles only, through the binding's custom properties; no literal colours, radii, shadows, durations or z-indexes (`#7c3aed`, `oklch(…)`, `border-radius: 12px`, `z-index: 50`, `300ms`).
resolved.rationale: Tokens are the primer; the component is the finish. A literal value breaks every theme at once.

detect.static: A declaration on a component part sets colour, radius, shadow, duration or z-index to anything other than `var(--lq-…)` (or a utility class that does not resolve to a role through the binding).

resolved.fix: Replace with the role's custom property from the binding (see spec/bindings/html.yaml).

resolved.title: Parts are addressable
resolved.statement: Every anatomy part renders with `data-slot="<part>"` so docs, tests and the grader can target it without classes.

detect.static: For each anatomy part marked required, an element with that data-slot exists.

resolved.fix: Add data-slot to the part's root element.

states.a11y: enabled, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, skeleton, invalid, empty
rules.local (three or more, at least one forbid)

detect.static: For each state the component declares, the matching attribute (aria-selected, aria-expanded, aria-invalid, aria-busy, aria-current, aria-checked) is present when the state is active.

resolved.fix: Set the attribute the APG pattern specifies; do not invent a new one.

resolved.title: Never remove focus without replacing it
resolved.statement: No `outline: none` / `outline-0` / `focus:outline-none` without a `:focus-visible` replacement that has ≥3:1 contrast against both the component and the page.

detect.static: Class or style removes outline and no focus-visible ring class/rule exists on the same element.
detect.runtime: Tab to the element; the focused and unfocused screenshots must differ at ≥3:1 along the element's edge.

resolved.fix: Use `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2` (or the binding's equivalent) and keep `:focus` untouched.

resolved.title: Native element first
resolved.statement: Prefer the native element (button, a, select, details, input) until a product requirement makes it impossible; a div or span with a click handler and a role is a defect unless the spec names an exception.

detect.static: div|span with onClick/onKeyDown and no native equivalent in the subtree.

resolved.fix: Replace with the native element; keep the styling.

resolved.title: Every control has an accessible name
resolved.statement: Every interactive element has an accessible name from content, a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; placeholder text and title attributes do not count.

detect.static: Compute the accessible name per accname 1.2; empty is a failure.

resolved.fix: Add visible text, a <label>, or aria-label for icon-only controls.

resolved.title: No literal values
resolved.statement: Component styles read token roles only, through the binding's custom properties; no literal colours, radii, shadows, durations or z-indexes (`#7c3aed`, `oklch(…)`, `border-radius: 12px`, `z-index: 50`, `300ms`).
resolved.rationale: Tokens are the primer; the component is the finish. A literal value breaks every theme at once.

detect.static: A declaration on a component part sets colour, radius, shadow, duration or z-index to anything other than `var(--lq-…)` (or a utility class that does not resolve to a role through the binding).

resolved.fix: Replace with the role's custom property from the binding (see spec/bindings/html.yaml).

resolved.title: Parts are addressable
resolved.statement: Every anatomy part renders with `data-slot="<part>"` so docs, tests and the grader can target it without classes.

detect.static: For each anatomy part marked required, an element with that data-slot exists.

resolved.fix: Add data-slot to the part's root element.

resolved.rationale: Most "the UI looks unfinished" complaints are missing states, not missing components.

detect.static: For each interactive element, the stylesheet or class list defines treatments for :hover, :focus-visible, :active and [disabled] / [aria-disabled].
detect.runtime: Drive each state and diff computed styles against the enabled state; each must differ in at least one property.

resolved.fix: Add the missing state using the component's token deltas (see its states[] treatment).

resolved.title: No state by colour alone
resolved.statement: No state is expressed by colour alone; every state has a second channel (icon, weight, border, position or text).

detect.static: A state's class delta changes only color/background-color.
detect.runtime: Grayscale the screenshot of each state and check it still differs from enabled.

resolved.fix: Add an icon, border, weight or text change alongside the colour change.

resolved.title: Every state reaches the accessibility tree
resolved.statement: Every visible state has an ARIA expression or an explicit "none" in the spec; selected, expanded, invalid, busy and current are never visual-only.

detect.static: For each state the component declares, the matching attribute (aria-selected, aria-expanded, aria-invalid, aria-busy, aria-current, aria-checked) is present when the state is active.

resolved.fix: Set the attribute the APG pattern specifies; do not invent a new one.

resolved.title: Never remove focus without replacing it
resolved.statement: No `outline: none` / `outline-0` / `focus:outline-none` without a `:focus-visible` replacement that has ≥3:1 contrast against both the component and the page.

detect.static: Class or style removes outline and no focus-visible ring class/rule exists on the same element.
detect.runtime: Tab to the element; the focused and unfocused screenshots must differ at ≥3:1 along the element's edge.

resolved.fix: Use `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2` (or the binding's equivalent) and keep `:focus` untouched.

resolved.title: Native element first
resolved.statement: Prefer the native element (button, a, select, details, input) until a product requirement makes it impossible; a div or span with a click handler and a role is a defect unless the spec names an exception.

detect.static: div|span with onClick/onKeyDown and no native equivalent in the subtree.

resolved.fix: Replace with the native element; keep the styling.

resolved.title: Every control has an accessible name
resolved.statement: Every interactive element has an accessible name from content, a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; placeholder text and title attributes do not count.

detect.static: Compute the accessible name per accname 1.2; empty is a failure.

resolved.fix: Add visible text, a <label>, or aria-label for icon-only controls.

resolved.title: No literal values
resolved.statement: Component styles read token roles only, through the binding's custom properties; no literal colours, radii, shadows, durations or z-indexes (`#7c3aed`, `oklch(…)`, `border-radius: 12px`, `z-index: 50`, `300ms`).
resolved.rationale: Tokens are the primer; the component is the finish. A literal value breaks every theme at once.

detect.static: A declaration on a component part sets colour, radius, shadow, duration or z-index to anything other than `var(--lq-…)` (or a utility class that does not resolve to a role through the binding).

resolved.fix: Replace with the role's custom property from the binding (see spec/bindings/html.yaml).

resolved.title: Parts are addressable
resolved.statement: Every anatomy part renders with `data-slot="<part>"` so docs, tests and the grader can target it without classes.

detect.static: For each anatomy part marked required, an element with that data-slot exists.

resolved.fix: Add data-slot to the part's root element.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: Modal window that interrupts the flow for a focused task and traps focus until dismissed.

anatomy.description: Full-viewport backdrop in color.bg.scrim. Click-to-close is a choice, not a default; destructive confirms disable it.
The container. role="dialog" aria-modal="true". Prefer the native `<dialog>` with showModal(); it provides the top layer and inertness for free.
Labels the dialog via aria-labelledby. Required. States the task, not the product ("Rename project", not "Project").
Icon button with aria-label="Close". Omit for dialogs that must be answered (see alert-dialog).
The scroll region when content overflows; the header and footer stay fixed.
Actions, right-aligned on desktop, stacked on mobile; the primary action is last in DOM and visual order.
Behavioural part. Tab cycles inside the dialog while open.

variants.guidance: Width only. Height follows content up to a viewport-relative max, then the body scrolls.
Non-modal dialogs do not trap focus or use a scrim; they are for tool palettes, not tasks.

states.treatment: color.bg.surface, radius.surface, shadow.lg, z.modal; scrim at color.bg.scrim.
states.a11y: role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby=<title id>. Everything behind it is inert.

states.treatment: Entry motion of motion.duration.base — fade + 2–4% scale, opacity-only under reduced motion.
states.a11y: Focus moves in on open; announcement is the title.

states.treatment: aria-busy on the body; footer actions keep width (see button loading).
Standard ring on every focusable inside; the dialog container itself is not focused unless nothing inside is.
none on the container; close-button and footer buttons own their own.
none on the container.
Dialogs are not disabled; actions inside may be.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Whether Escape and scrim-click close it. False for confirms that need an explicit answer.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: Where focus lands on open. Default is the first focusable element; for destructive confirms, the cancel button.

api.composition: Trigger, Title, Description, Body and Footer are composed as children so any content works and headings stay real headings. Size and modality are props because the system owns those sets. Do not add `confirmLabel` / `onConfirm` props; that is alert-dialog.

accessibility.name: aria-labelledby pointing at the title; aria-describedby at the description when present.

keyboard.action: Cycles focus within the dialog; never escapes to the page.

accessibility.focus: On open, focus moves to initialFocus, else the first focusable, else the container (tabindex=-1). On close, focus returns to the element that opened it. If that element is gone, focus the nearest logical ancestor.
accessibility.announcements: The title is announced on open by virtue of focus movement; no extra live region.

content.label: Title is the task as a verb phrase ("Rename project", "Invite teammates"). Footer buttons name the outcome ("Rename", "Send invites"), never "OK".
content.limits: One paragraph of description at most; longer content is a page, not a dialog.

use_when: A short task must be completed or abandoned before the user continues.
The user needs to confirm something with consequences (use alert-dialog for the destructive case).
avoid_when: The content is long or deserves its own URL — use a page.
You are stacking dialogs — flatten into steps or use a drawer.
The content is contextual and non-blocking — use a popover.
On mobile with a long form — use a full-screen or bottom drawer.

instead.when: Destructive confirmation requiring an explicit answer
Side panel with the page still usable
Small contextual content anchored to a trigger

local.title: Focus in, focus back
local.statement: Opening moves focus inside the dialog; closing returns focus to the trigger.

detect.runtime: document.activeElement is inside the dialog after open and equals the trigger after close.

local.fix: Use the native <dialog>.showModal() or the renderer's focus-scope primitive; store the trigger on open.

local.title: Background is inert
local.statement: While a modal dialog is open, content outside it is inert (not focusable, not clickable, hidden from assistive tech).

detect.runtime: Tab from the last focusable inside wraps to the first; outside elements are not reachable.

local.fix: Use <dialog>.showModal() or set `inert` on siblings of the portal root.

local.title: Never an unlabeled dialog
local.statement: Every dialog has a visible title referenced by aria-labelledby; a visually-hidden title is acceptable only for full-screen media viewers.

detect.static: role=dialog without aria-labelledby, or the referenced element is empty.

local.title: Destructive confirms default to safety

detect.runtime: On open, activeElement is the cancel button when a destructive button is present.

local.fix: Set initialFocus to the cancel action and dismissible=false.

resolved.title: All five base states
resolved.statement: Every interactive component implements enabled, hover, focus-visible, active and disabled with a defined visual treatment, including in dark mode.
resolved.rationale: Most "the UI looks unfinished" complaints are missing states, not missing components.

detect.static: For each interactive element, the stylesheet or class list defines treatments for :hover, :focus-visible, :active and [disabled] / [aria-disabled].
detect.runtime: Drive each state and diff computed styles against the enabled state; each must differ in at least one property.

resolved.fix: Add the missing state using the component's token deltas (see its states[] treatment).

resolved.title: No state by colour alone
resolved.statement: No state is expressed by colour alone; every state has a second channel (icon, weight, border, position or text).

detect.static: A state's class delta changes only color/background-color.
detect.runtime: Grayscale the screenshot of each state and check it still differs from enabled.

resolved.fix: Add an icon, border, weight or text change alongside the colour change.

resolved.title: Every state reaches the accessibility tree
resolved.statement: Every visible state has an ARIA expression or an explicit "none" in the spec; selected, expanded, invalid, busy and current are never visual-only.

detect.static: For each state the component declares, the matching attribute (aria-selected, aria-expanded, aria-invalid, aria-busy, aria-current, aria-checked) is present when the state is active.

resolved.fix: Set the attribute the APG pattern specifies; do not invent a new one.

resolved.title: Never remove focus without replacing it
resolved.statement: No `outline: none` / `outline-0` / `focus:outline-none` without a `:focus-visible` replacement that has ≥3:1 contrast against both the component and the page.

detect.static: Class or style removes outline and no focus-visible ring class/rule exists on the same element.
detect.runtime: Tab to the element; the focused and unfocused screenshots must differ at ≥3:1 along the element's edge.

resolved.fix: Use `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2` (or the binding's equivalent) and keep `:focus` untouched.

resolved.title: Native element first
resolved.statement: Prefer the native element (button, a, select, details, input) until a product requirement makes it impossible; a div or span with a click handler and a role is a defect unless the spec names an exception.

detect.static: div|span with onClick/onKeyDown and no native equivalent in the subtree.

resolved.fix: Replace with the native element; keep the styling.

resolved.title: Every control has an accessible name
resolved.statement: Every interactive element has an accessible name from content, a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; placeholder text and title attributes do not count.

detect.static: Compute the accessible name per accname 1.2; empty is a failure.

resolved.fix: Add visible text, a <label>, or aria-label for icon-only controls.

resolved.title: No literal values

resolved.title: Parts are addressable
resolved.statement: Every anatomy part renders with `data-slot="<part>"` so docs, tests and the grader can target it without classes.

detect.static: For each anatomy part marked required, an element with that data-slot exists.

resolved.fix: Add data-slot to the part's root element.

resolved.title: Never remove focus without replacing it
